We count on the continued solidarity of our partners and the guidance of ECOSOC to realize this vision. Madam President, Timor-Leste also welcomes the progress in negotiations toward a UN framework convention on international tax cooperation, a milestone initiative toward a fairer, more inclusive global tax architecture. Strengthening international tax cooperation will help developing countries mobilize domestic resources an essential condition for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. Finally, Madam President, as we prepare for the mid-term review of the Doha Programme of Action for LDCs, Timor-Leste calls upon ECOSOC to champion a new approach, one that transforms vulnerability into resilience. Timor-Leste reaffirms its unwavering commitment to multilateralism, and with the new President of ECOSOC, to fulfill the collective promise of the United Nations to leave no one behind. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Timor-Leste. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Portugal.

Madam President, Portugal aligns itself with the statement delivered by the European Union. Allow me to begin by echoing warmly and deliberately the tributes expressed today to Ambassador Bob Ray for his exemplary leadership of the Economic and Social Council. His vision, energy and unwavering political commitment have marked this ECOSOC cycle in a profound way. As is clear from the interventions we have just heard, he leaves behind a legacy of clarity, purpose, and integrity. And may I add in a personal note and quoting his quotation of Sonnet 25 of William Shakespeare, that I'm sure that he will also remain beloved here where he was or will be removed. We would like also to congratulate Ambassador Lok Bahadur Thapa as he assumes the presidency of the Council. Portugal looks forward to working closely with him as the United Nations system navigates a decisive moment in implementing the 2030 Agenda and the Pact for the Future. Excellencies, the report of the ECOSOC provides a comprehensive and substantive picture of a year marked by intense multilateral engagement. From the operational activities segment to the high-level political forum, from the special meetings on tax cooperation and artificial intelligence to the joint and important sessions on Haiti and on forced displacement. It also reaffirms the indispensable role of the United Nations Sustainable Development pillar, an irreplaceable one within the United Nations, and of ECOSOC as a central platform for coordinating the organization's socioeconomic work, which lies at the heart of implementing the 2030 Agenda. Allow me now to highlight three points particularly relevant from Portugal's perspective. First of all, financing for development remains the backbone of our collective ability to deliver on the SDGs. In this regard, and as former co-chairs of the Preparatory Committee for FfD 4, Portugal wishes to pay a special tribute to Canada and personally to Ambassador Bob Ray for his exceptional engagement and leadership in this file. He consistently went beyond rhetoric, taking concrete steps to deepen the membership's understanding of the challenges and opportunities in financing sustainable development. And he did so as co-chair of the Group of Friends on SDG Financing, but also equally as President of ECOSOC. Perhaps most importantly, he helped narrow the long-noted gap between the cities of Washington and New York, a structural challenge in the financing for development agenda. This contribution, we are sure, will endure. ECOSOC's dedicated FFD forum remains an essential platform to advance a more inclusive global financial architecture, enhance international tax cooperation, and strengthen access to affordable finance for the most vulnerable. Second, Ambassador Ray's leadership was consistently guided by principles, never shying away from reaffirming the centrality of human rights, of gender equality, and of the empowerment of women and girls as indispensable foundations for sustainable development. These values are not additional add-ons. They are preconditions for success. Portugal deeply appreciates his moral clarity in consistently upholding these guiding elements, particularly at a moment when consensus is increasingly fragile. Third. ECOSOC's work during this cycle reinforced the importance of evidence-based policy, science, innovation and future thinking. This is reflected in the High-Level Political Forum, the STI Forum and the Council's emphasis on long-term trends, digital transformation and artificial intelligence, including the need to harness AI responsibly to accelerate sustainable development while addressing its risks. These are essential discussions as the UN approaches its 80th anniversary and prepares for the next cycle of implementation of the 2030 Agenda. Excellencies, to conclude, at the midway point between the adoption of the SDGs and the 2030 horizon, and in the first year of implementing the Pact for the Future, ECOSOC's role is more vital than ever. Delivering coherence, mobilizing political attention, and ensuring system-wide accountability will remain central tasks. Portugal stands ready to support the new President in a new cycle in the ECOSOC and to continue working with all partners to rebuild trust, strengthen multilateral action and accelerate the implementation of the SDGs. Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Portugal. We've heard the last speaker in the debate on these items. May I take it that the Assembly takes note of the report of the Economic and Social Council? It is so decided. The Assembly has thus concluded this stage of its consideration of agenda items 9 and 13. The Assembly will begin its consideration in a joint debate of agenda item 120, entitled "Implementation of the resolutions of the United Nations", and agenda item 121, entitled "Revitalization of the work of the General Assembly". I will now make a statement as the President of the General Assembly on that item. Excellencies, Let me begin by recognizing the leadership of Ambassador Corneliu Furuta, Permanent Representative of Romania, and Ambassador Matu Jojini, Permanent Representative of South Africa, as former co-chairs of the Ad Hoc Working Group on the Revitalization of the Work of the General Assembly. Revitalization remains central to the strength and credibility of this Assembly. We thank you both, dear Ambassadors, Your Excellencies, for your stewardship of this process during the previous session. Today, the revitalization process unfolds against the backdrop of a broader reform agenda, the UN80 initiative. These two efforts are intertwined. Both aim to make the United Nations more effective, more efficient, and ultimately stronger. As a chief deliberative, policy-making and representative organ of the UN, the General Assembly must lead by example, showing that it too can adapt to the challenges of the 21st century. Business as usual will not suffice. We need fewer repetitive resolutions, shorter debates and smarter scheduling. No more resolutions for resolutions' sake. Only resolutions that propel our work, that deliver on the UN's mission to promote peace, development, and human rights. By optimizing our methods and processes, we can work smarter, deliver faster, and ensure that every decision of this Assembly drives real impact. Resolution 79/327 charts the course. It calls on each main committee to review its working methods and propose concrete measures to enhance efficiency, including merging similar agenda items to avoid repetition, reducing the frequency, length, and number of resolutions, using biennial and triennial cycles where appropriate. by limiting explanations of vote to five minutes, and simplifying adoption procedures, one gavel, one decision, all texts. These recommendations, so your recommendations, recommendations by member states, would help shape a General Assembly that is not mired in bureaucracy, but equipped to respond to global challenges with agility and coherence, An Assembly ready for the scale of its responsibilities. But unless these reforms are implemented, they remain just words on paper. Just another resolution. Colleagues, on this I must be candid. We cannot preach on Sunday that we need fewer resolutions, then proceed to submit one for consideration on Monday. And this is unfortunately taking place. We have seen the main committees put forward resolutions for three-day conferences with no budget attached, fully aware of the fiscal situation we are debating at the same moment. We have seen over 160 side events during High-Level Week, despite the call for less, or by some even the call for no side events at all. And we have seen already three or four high-level meetings submitted for consideration for the 81st High-Level Week, with four for each of the 82nd and 83rd, despite the decision of this Assembly, so by all of us, to limit this to a maximum of three. While we all want to protect the things we care about, Each of us must make concessions in this time of reform. If we do not make the hard decisions, others, less passionate about or even in opposition to this institution, to its mission and its mandates, will make decisions for us. This holds true also for the Office of the President of the General Assembly. As underlined also in the resolution, the workload and expectations placed upon this body grow, so too do those placed upon the President and their office. Revitalization must therefore extend to the OPGJ itself. And the 80th session benefited from an early, seamless handover from the 79th, allowing us to hit the ground running. Yet the volume of work remains immense. Our high-level week featured over seven major meetings in just a few days. The remainder of the session will see nearly 20 intergovernmental processes and multiple mandated high-level meetings. And the total number of resolutions has barely changed, many nearly indigental to those of past sessions. Colleagues, again, this is not sustainable. and it's contradicting the call, especially from smaller missions, that they cannot be at three meetings at the same time. So transitions matter. Preparation matters. We must ensure each presidency is set up for success. I therefore thank all member states who have supported and continue to support the OPGA during this session. I encourage continued investments in the OPGA Trust Fund and the Fellowship Program, and sustained attention to policies that strengthen this office to meet the growing demands. Excellencies, dear colleagues, we all know the months ahead will be demanding. So it needs all of us, and it needs our team spirit. We are, indeed, better together. The UN AIDS initiative, while spearheaded by the Secretary General, increasingly depends on you, the membership, your engagement, sometimes your personal engagement, like we just discussed in the other session. Likewise, the selection process for the next Secretary-General must be a shared priority by all of us, given the important role played by the Secretary-General in the context of current global challenges. The revitalization resolutions have introduced significant improvements to the selection and appointment process of the Secretary-General, and the UN membership has provided clear guidance therein. Resolution 79/327 defines the principles and process steps for the upcoming selection and appointment. I am working closely with the President of the Security Council to ensure that this process is inclusive and transparent, in line with Resolution 79/327, including the joint letter inviting Member States to present candidates. I look forward to working with you as this process unfolds. Excellencies, whether on reform, budgets or procedures, difficult decisions lie ahead. Our task is to ensure that this Assembly is ready to meet them, every day. Revitalization is not procedural housekeeping. It is institutional renewal. Let us work together to define a General Assembly that is not repetitive, fragmented or procedural, but a General Assembly that is strategic, coherent and focused on outcomes. A General Assembly that is better together. I thank you. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of our next session. which is Slovenia, please. The floor is yours.

Thank you, Madam President. And thank you for very clear messages and your call to honor all of us to align our actions with the resolutions that we are adopting. Now I have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of Mexico, Spain, and my own country, Slovenia. Madam President, Thank you for convening this plenary meeting on the issue of General Assembly revitalization during the 80th session. First of all, we would like to thank the co-chairs of the ad hoc working group on the revitalization of the work of the General Assembly during its 79th session, the permanent representative of the Republic of South Africa, Ambassador Matu Joyni, and Romania, Ambassador Cornel Feruta. the ad hoc working group under your leadership deliver an outcome with a number of important achievements. Madam President, a year ago on this very podium, Slovenia, together with Mexico and Spain, and joined by a group of 79 other member states, delivered a statement highlighting the importance of gender equality and the representation of women in leadership positions at the United Nations. We continued our engagement towards greater gender parity throughout the session, together with a large group of like-minded States. The strong support of the wider membership to the message on the importance of gender balance and parity resulted in the adoption of key provisions within resolution 79/327. We welcome the provisions on the representation of women and gender balance in the top two most visible leadership positions. We see it as progress towards facilitating more equal representation of women and men in UN leadership, but much more remains to be done. Madam President, your election as the only fifth woman ever to serve as the President of the General Assembly is historic. However, it also reminds us that in the 80 years of our organization, only a handful of women have presided over the General Assembly, and no woman has ever held the position of the UN Secretary-General. These facts are not only regrettable, they are unacceptable. We therefore look towards forward to seeing more women put forward as candidates for both the President of the General Assembly and the Secretary-General, and we urge Member States to uphold the principle of gender balance throughout the nomination, selection and appointment processes. At the same time, we call on Member States to consider additional measures to close the persistent gender gap. In line with resolution 79/327, we look forward to exploring concrete steps to address the gender disparity in the position of the President of the General Assembly at the 81st session. One such step could be an arrangement on the rotation between men and women in this important role. But no matter what formula or mechanism we agree on, the outcome must be clear: an agreement among Member States on a procedure to ensure gender parity in future selection processes for all UN leadership positions. Madam President, the urgency of this issue is undeniable. The United Nations is facing uncertain and challenging times. To take us forward, we need to take advantage of all the talent, experience and potential of the people the UN represents. including half of the global population that has so far been too often excluding from leading it. Underrepresentation of women has no place in modern societies, political decision-making, or multilateralism. Real change is not only necessary, but has long been overdue. Madam President, some changes take time, but others require bold and immediate action. Now is the moment to be bold, to demand concrete action and results, both within the revitalization process and beyond. Let's make sure the UN leads by example and demonstrate our collective commitment to gender equality through the full, equal and meaningful participation of women at the highest levels of decision-making. Let's end the 80th session of the General Assembly with a woman President of the General Assembly and incoming woman Secretary-General. I thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Slovenia on behalf of Mexico and Spain. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the European Union on behalf of the EU and its Member States.

Madam President, Excellencies, Distinguished Delegates, I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the European Union and its Member States. The candidate countries North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, Albania, Ukraine, the Republic of Moldova, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Georgia, as well as San Marino, align themselves with this statement. The European Union attaches great importance to the full and effective implementation of General Assembly resolutions and to the revitalization of the work of this body. We view these efforts as essential to ensuring that the General Assembly remains an efficient, transparent, and credible pillar of multilateralism, capable of responding to the complex challenges facing the United Nations and the international community. The European Union welcomes the progress made at the outset of the 80th session in implementing commitments across the main committees, as outlined in resolution 79/327. GA revitalization remains central to the UN80 initiative and closely linked to its work. We look forward to seeing how synergies develop between this process and the ongoing efforts across the three UN80 work streams. We encourage active engagement between the bureaus and the informal ad hoc working group on the mandate implementation review.

We also look forward to the implementation of the agreed language on cluster 3 of the resolution on revitalization concerning the selection and appointment of the Secretary-General. This will be an important milestone of this session and should contribute to a more transparent and inclusive process, in line with Article 97 of the Charter. Madam President, please allow me to briefly summarise the work of the main committees. On the first committee, the first committee completed its work ahead of schedule despite fewer meetings and more statements. demonstrating that streamlining is possible. New time limits, effective time management and organisational innovations, such as disclosing the identity of states requesting votes in writing, have proven essential. On the second committee, revitalisation remains vital to strengthen effectiveness and ensure delivery of the 2030 agenda. Inaction and fragmented efforts threaten progress on the sustainable development goals. We cannot afford to lose momentum. This committee must drive efficiency, coherence and impact. Consideration should be given to the number and timing of resolutions to reflect shared priorities and maximise impact. Switching to Spanish. On the third committee, reduced meeting time was managed efficiently by combining general debates, which freed approximately 15 hours. We commend this innovative approach and encourage its continuation, alongside measures like reducing the length and periodicity of resolutions. On the fourth committee, communicating changes to the programme of work via e-delegates enhanced transparency and predictability. Starting substantive work immediately and using a table format programme of work improved the use of time and the quality of the discussions. On the fifth committee, revitalisation is timely and necessary. The current programme of work does not fully reflect the committee's scope and complexity. Systemic review of the causes behind repeated extensions and lost time in resume sessions is needed. Rationalisation and enhanced working methods would improve predictability, efficiency and cost effectiveness. The sixth committee now. Here, the European Union has proposed streamlining, for example, the resolution on the report of the special committee on the Charter of the United Nations and on the strengthening of the role of the organization by condensing 13 preambular paragraphs, which recall earlier reports and resolutions that go back as far as 1995 into a single reference. While discussions continue, this illustrates the benefits of shortening products, improving readability, and selecting only relevant references. In conclusion, we shouldn't go the easy way of technical rollovers, but instead critically assess each paragraph and reference and delete outdated elements.

Madam President, revitalization is a continuous effort that requires institutional adjustments, political will, and accountability. The European Union reaffirms its commitment to constructive engagement for a more effective, transparent and inclusive General Assembly. We stand ready to contribute to discussions that ensure the UN's deliberative bodies remain efficient, credible and responsible to the needs of the international community. I thank you.
I thank the Distinguished Representative of the European Union. I now give the floor to the Distinguished Representative of Australia on behalf of CANS.

Thank you, President, and thank you very much indeed to our colleagues from Romania and South Africa for the hard work undertaken over the course of the period in relation to revitalization. As the President mentioned, I speak on behalf of Canada, New Zealand, and of course, my own country, Australia. In a system too often challenged by division, the unique convening power of the General Assembly as a forum for all Member States, big and small, remains unmatched. The adoption of resolution 79/327 by consensus demonstrates that Member States believe in and want an effective General Assembly. Reform has always been part of the United Nations conversation. But today, with growing global challenges and even more limited resources, it's more urgent than ever. Revitalization is a crucial mechanism to make the General Assembly function better so that it delivers more. We are committed to a strong, efficient and streamlined General Assembly. In this regard, revitalization goes hand in hand with the Secretary-General's UN80 reform initiative. Today, CAHNS makes three key points. First, we welcome resolution 79/327 as a strong step in the right direction and encourage all member states to walk the talk and support its full implementation. For example, the resolution prioritizes efficiency through the one gavel approach to adopting consensus main committee resolutions, by encouraging members to keep explanations of vote to under five minutes, and by pausing new proposals for international days, weeks, months, and years, and decades, and grouping together future commemorative resolutions. These practices will help the General Assembly focus on the key issues that matter most and can make it easier for all Member States, particularly small and medium-sized delegations, meaningfully to engage in the work of the Assembly. Second, looking forward, Cairns encourages all of us to carry momentum forward and to continue to advance the unfinished business of General Assembly revitalization, to include time-bound provisions or at least mandate review clauses when they are appropriate in new General Assembly resolutions, to assess resource implications and program budget implications early in the establishment or renewal of mandates and to identify appropriate offsets where needed; to promote multi-annual renewal for General Assembly resolutions that do not substantively change from year to year; and to encourage the President of the General Assembly to provide action-oriented recommendations regarding the use of the veto, as requested in resolution 79/327, to realize the potential of the veto initiative in increasing transparency and accountability around the use of the veto. Third, CANS welcomes the establishment of the Working Group on the Strengthening and Revitalizing the Work of the General Assembly and calls for the new Working Group to coordinate closely with the UNAT informal ad hoc Working Group on Mandates under Workstream 2, including ways that the General Assembly Revitalization Working Group could build upon and implement the outcomes of the informal ad hoc Working Group to improve the creation, implementation and review of resolutions. We also welcome each of the six main committees reviewing their working methods this session and submitting concrete proposals to the General Committee on how to make their work more efficient and effective, while also ensuring coordination with ongoing work under UNAT Work Stream 2 to avoid duplication of efforts and ensure coherence across committee work. In closing, CAN supports continuing to work towards a revitalized and resilient General Assembly, because a more effective and efficient General Assembly is crucial to creating a United Nations that is capable of solving the world's problems for generations to come. Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Australia on behalf of Cairns. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Malaysia on behalf of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

Thank you, Madam President. Malaysia has the honor of speaking on behalf of the 11 members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, as its chair for this year. At the outset, ASEAN wishes to thank Ambassador Corneliu Furuta of Romania and Ambassador Mathu Joyini of South Africa for their stewardship as the co-chairs of the ad hoc working group on the revitalization of the work of the General Assembly during the 79th session. Madam President, we welcome the adoption by consensus of the resolution on the revitalization of the work of the General Assembly at the previous session. ASEAN believes the resolution will continue to contribute and strengthen our collective efforts on the important agenda of revitalizing the General Assembly. ASEAN has actively participated and contributed to the thematic debates convened by the Co-Chairs during the 79th session. During the thematic debates, ASEAN consistently advocated for greater women's representation for the positions of the President of the General Assembly and of the Secretary-General of the UN. We have also urged for the strengthening of the institutional memory of the Office of the President of the General Assembly and for its adequate funding and support. ASEAN will continue this active engagement and contribution during the current session. Madam President, to contribute to this plenary debate, allow me to emphasize the following points. First, ASEAN welcomes efforts to streamline and further strengthen the working methods of the General Assembly as provided by the resolution on the revitalization of the work of the General Assembly. The reformed working methods, if fully implemented, will allow for better optimization of resources for both Member States and the UN. It is important that all Member States work together to ensure the reforms to the working method under the resolution are fully implemented. We are encouraged by and fully support the continued emphasis on equal and fair geographical representation to ensure that our regions are fairly represented in the leadership roles of the UN. Geographical balance and distribution are essential in the selection and appointment of the Secretary-General and among executive heads within the UN. This geographical balance and rotation should receive our continued support to strengthen a just and inclusive system. The previous point about geographical balance brings me to an equally, if not more important matter, the under-representation of women in leadership positions within the UN. We currently have a woman elected as the PGA, but sadly, she is only the fifth out of 80 PGAs since the establishment of the UN. Even more deserving of our attention, no woman has ever been the UN Secretary General. ASEAN reiterates our call to encourage the nomination of women candidates for the positions of the PGA, the Secretary-General, and other executive heads of the UN. We must translate our commitment to gender equality into concrete actions through appointments to these important positions. Madam President, to conclude, ASEAN remains dedicated to advancing the revitalization of the work of the General Assembly agenda. We look forward to working closely with the co-chairs and contributing constructively alongside member states to further advance the bold reforms required to renew the General Assembly's central role in global governance, ensuring it remains an effective, inclusive and accountable institution. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Malaysia. On behalf of ASEAN, I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Algeria on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement.

Madam President, I have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement, one of the largest cross-regional groups consisting of 121 member states. The movement reaffirms its strong commitment to strengthening the central role of the General Assembly as the most representative, democratic, and universal organ of the United Nations, ensuring that the General Assembly remains the primary forum for multilateral dialogue and decision-making is vital for a more inclusive and effective United Nations. The Non-Aligned Movement emphasizes that the revitalization of the General Assembly is a critical component of the comprehensive reform of the United Nations. It should aim to enhance its authority and its efficiency while preserving its intergovernmental nature. The Non-Aligned Movement welcomes the progress reflected in Resolution 79/327, which demonstrates Member States' commitment to a more efficient and revitalized General Assembly and to revigorating the multilateral system. In this regard, the Movement attaches great importance to maintaining a transparent, inclusive and Member State-driven process within the Working Group on the strengthening and revitalizing of the work of the General Assembly. Revitalization must not be viewed as a mere procedural exercise, but as a political process that enhances the Assembly's role. The participation of all states, particularly developing countries, must remain central to the process of improving the working methods and agenda of the Assembly. The Movement stressed the need for balanced and coordinated interaction between the General Assembly, the Security Council, and the ECOSOC, in strict conformity with the UN Charter. The Assembly should continue to exercise its full competence on matters of peace and security, of development, and of human rights, in accordance with the Charter, and ensuring that its resolutions and debates contribute meaningfully to the work of the United Nations as a whole. In this context, the movement emphasized the UN80 initiative, while offering an opportunity to strengthen the multilateral system, should not divert attention or resources away from the core priorities of developing countries. The Non-Aligned Movement further underlines the importance of promoting gender balance, equitable geographical representation, and multilingualism within the UN system, including in senior positions. In this regard, the Movement reiterates that the process for the selection and appointment of the Secretary-General of the United Nations and other executive heads must remain transparent, must remain inclusive with geographical balance and guided by the principles of equality and merit, continuing efforts to achieve fair distribution in terms of gender and geographical balance, noting that that has yet to be a woman Secretary-General, and emphasizing the importance of continuing efforts to achieve geographical balance. The movement further stresses the need to strengthen the office of the President of the General Assembly, including through enhanced transparency institutional continuity, and adequate resources from regular budget in order to ensure its impartiality, efficiency, and capacity to fulfill its important mandate. Madam President, the Non-Aligned Movement remains firmly committed to a revitalized General Assembly, A General Assembly that upholds the principles of equality, universality and multilateralism, ensuring that the voices of all Member States, especially developing countries, are heard and are respected. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Algeria on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Estonia on behalf of the ACT Group.

President, I'm honored to take the floor on behalf of our 27 members of Accountability, Coherence, and Transparency ACT Group. First, we would like to thank the co-chairs of ad hoc working group on the revitalization of the General Assembly of the last session. Ambassadors, Colonel Ferruta and Matujoyeni, and their teams for their committed efforts on the negotiations of a resolution adopted in September. Our group is looking forward to continue working towards a more efficient, transparent, and inclusive General Assembly at a time when the United Nations is at the crossroads, politically as well as financially. President, the most pressing issue the United Nations faces today pertains to peace and security. Act Group has always maintained that, in line with Chapter VIII of the Charter, the General Assembly has a clear and active role to play in this area, a role we have seen becoming even more important, especially when the Security Council is unable to act. In this regard, we are pleased to see that Resolution 79/327 recognizes the functions, powers and role of the Assembly in a more detailed manner. enhancing thereby the fulfillment of GA's responsibilities in matters of international peace and security. We have seen the relevance of emergency special session and the veto initiative in ensuring better accountability within the United Nations system and strengthening the role of Assembly. We believe that there are more opportunities for the GA's active role within these frameworks, including making concrete recommendations to Member States or the Security Council, as empowered by Articles 10, 11 and 12 of the Charter. Another valuable resource for equipping the Assembly to take on its role is the Assembly for Peace Digital Handbook. We encourage all Member States to make full use of it. We hope, President, that your office will continue with its annual update and wider dissemination among Member States, as encouraged in resolution 79/327. We are pleased that the GA revitalization resolution reconfirms the commitment made in the Pact for the Future to support credible, timely and decisive action by the Security Council to prevent or end the commission of genocide, crimes against humanity or war crimes and reiterates the call to member states to refrain from measures impeding such action, including by the misuse of the veto. We encourage the current 130 signatories to the ACT Code of Conduct to consistently adhere to their responsibilities and call for more countries to join the Code of Conduct. We especially encourage signatories on the Council to work together to initiate relevant discussions and products. That group highlights the importance of ensuring the application of Article 27 of the UN Charter, which includes the obligation that members of the Security Council abstain from voting on decisions under Chapter VI and under paragraph 3 of Article 52 if they are party to a dispute. Past years, in particular, have seen clear cases of non-observance of this obligatory Charter provision. the Council must fully implement and adhere again to this important provision. The failure to implement it directly affects the effectiveness of the United Nations and contradicts the no one is the judge in their own cause principle. We believe that the General Assembly has a role in ensuring observance of the Charter and look forward to working with all those with an interest in taking action to this end. President, the Security Council's annual report to the GA serves as an important transparency and accountability measure on the work of the Security Council in fulfilling their mandate to maintain international peace and security. While we welcome the Security Council's efforts in producing a more comprehensive annual report and the inclusion of a chapter on special reports on the use of the veto, we continue to encourage the Council to provide a more complete substantive, and analytical account of its work to the General Assembly, one that goes beyond a factual summary to include assessment of trends, outcomes of decisions, and the impact of implementation on the ground, including an analysis of the cases in which the veto has been exercised. President, in 2026, the General Assembly will appoint the next Secretary-General for this organization. Resolution 79/327 made some progress both for the Assembly and the Security Council in advancing the process of a selection of a Secretary-General. Whilst ACT is pleased that for the first time the resolution sets out the general timeline for the role process, We encourage more details in the forthcoming joint letter from Presidents of the Security Council and the General Assembly on the timing for different stages of the process in both the Council and the Assembly. The predictability of a timeframe for the process is an important transparency measure that eases procedural burdens and improves clarity of the process for Member States, civil society, and candidates alike. Furthermore, given the multitude of issues and challenges facing the Organization, not least the ongoing UN80 reform process, the next SG needs to have sufficient time to prepare for the office. So we hope the joint letter will be issued soon. ACT reiterates the importance of interactive hearings of the General Assembly with candidates, which are enriched by the full and meaningful participation of civil society. We also encourage the continuation of a successful town hall held in 2016. The race for the next SG must stretch beyond Turtle Bay. We should not miss an opportunity to enhance public interest and engagement in the work of the UN and its next Secretary-General. AdGrUP also strongly encourages the Security Council to present two or more candidates for the consideration of the GA. and for the President of the General Assembly to consider ways to assess the level of GA support for the candidates throughout the process. This could be done through advisory votes or similar quantifiable mechanisms in order to indicate which candidates the wider membership may support, not support, or have no strong opinion on. This would ensure critical alignment between the two principal UN organs and enhance the complementary roles assigned to both forums in the Charter. Prior to its formal appointment decision, the General Assembly should also hold an additional interactive session with any candidate recommended by the Security Council, ensuring continued engagement with the membership. The resolution 79/327 rightly notes with regret that no woman has ever held the position of UN Secretary-General, and encourages Member States to strongly consider nominating women candidates. ACT strongly supports this call to Member States. After 80 years, we cannot miss the transformative opportunity and show our organization's commitment to gender equality at the highest level. I thank you, President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Estonia on behalf of the ACP Group. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Indonesia.

Madam President, Indonesia supports the statements made by Algeria on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement and Malaysia on behalf of the ASEAN countries. For Indonesia, revitalization is a question of purpose. Indonesia envisions a General Assembly that is not only fit for purpose, but also fit for the future. That is why we view the adoption of resolution 79/327 as a meaningful step forward in our shared mission. It reaffirms our conviction that the revitalization of this Assembly lies at the heart of broader UN reforms. The General Assembly must remain the moral compass and center of gravity of multilateralism, where every voice counts and every nation matters. Allow me, Madam President, to highlight three points. First, Indonesia welcomes the establishment of the Working Group on the Strengthening and Revitalization of the General Assembly. This institutional innovation is more than just a structural reform. It ensures that revitalization becomes a living process, dynamic, inclusive, and accountable. By operating on a triennial cycle, the working group brings continuity, coherence, and sense of ownership to the reform process. Secondly, Indonesia commends the stronger provisions in Resolution 79/327 that promotes transparency, integrity, and accountability, particularly in the selection process of the Secretary-General. The resolution codifies clear rules and timelines, one nomination per member state, disclosure of campaign funding, and measures to promote gender parity. Together with the Wisnumurti guidelines of 1996, they emphasize that the UN must embody the values of fairness, openness, and inclusivity. And third, Indonesia welcomes the new culture of discipline and efficiency introduced under this resolution. This includes limiting high-level meetings during high-level week, simplifying resolution adoption and procedures at the plenary, and putting on hold new proposals for international commemorations. These are pragmatic measures that bring coherence and focus to our work. Madam President, the progress embodied in resolution 79/327 resonates with the spirit of the Pact for the Future and the UN80 initiative. calling for a United Nation that is more responsive to present and future challenges. Revitalization is not about doing less, but about doing better. It is about streamlining without sidelining, reforming without fragmenting, and renewing without losing our founding vision. Indonesia remains committed to working with all Member States to ensure that revitalization is not merely a resolution adopted by consensus, but a consensus that delivers. Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative of Indonesia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Philippines.

Thank you, Madam President. The Philippines aligns itself with the statement delivered by Malaysia on behalf of ASEAN. I would now like to speak briefly in my national capacity and offer some other related topics and related points. Given the growing complexity of its agenda, the current financial situation of the United Nations, the evolving needs of Member States, and ongoing efforts to revitalize the General Assembly, a review of the Main Committee's working methods is needed to ensure that the committee's procedures enhance their effective, inclusive, and transparent work in responding to contemporary needs and challenges. Taking into account General Assembly resolution 79/327 on revitalization, some practical measures to improve the GA's working methods include enhancing the efficiency and inclusiveness of the committee's deliberations, strengthening coordination with other bodies, improving the implementation and follow-up of committee outcomes, and rationalizing side events and other similar activities. More specifically, I wish to propose improvements in four areas. One, streamlining the agenda and agenda management, namely, through consensus decisions on measures such as biennial or triennial consideration of selected agenda items, sunset mechanism for agenda items agreed, clustering related topics, and review criteria for the conduct of side events. Two, time management through uniform indicative time limits for interventions, if possible, a uniform time limits for all committees, including the time and number of the exercise of rights of reply. This may require amending parts of the General Assembly rules of procedures and rationalizing the length of presentation of the reports to the main committees by representatives of UN bodies and other agencies. Third, number three, Strengthening bureau functions through enhancing the roles and responsibilities of bureaus, including facilitators and coordinators, and early nomination of coordinators of resolutions and decisions to allow adequate preparation before the session and identifying the issues and agenda items that they will coordinate before the beginning of the work committees. Number four, improving transparency and documentation through developing a digital compendium of working methods and precedents for institutional memory and enhanced information sharing mechanism on the implementation of General Assembly resolutions. On implementation and follow-up of outcomes, the following are proposed or suggested. The adoption of the General Assembly of of a working methods paper or decision for the main committees while it would identify best practices and areas for improvement for the main committees. Establishing a regular, informal, open-ended working group or working methods to implement and work or working methods to review implementation using any agreed working methods decision as basis. And finally, that agreed working methods be implemented by all committees, subject to review and update every year by the General Assembly through the aforementioned informal open-ended working group. Thank you, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Philippines. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Saudi Arabia.

Madam President, at the outset, my delegation associates itself with the statement of Algeria on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. We extend our thanks to the Permanent Representative of South Africa and to the Permanent Representative of Romania for their efforts during the previous session of the GA. Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, amidst multifaceted challenges facing the international system, the role of the United Nations is more important than ever. The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia which as a founding member of the organization, attaches great importance to the revitalization of the works of the General Assembly. The GA is the main representative deliberative organ for policymaking in our organization. It is the symbol of multilateralism. The role of the General Assembly is wide and far-reaching. It covers political, security, economic, and social issues. It also covers administrative and financial aspects of the organization. The revitalization of the works of the General Assembly is an important step towards a comprehensive reform of the organization, hence the need for collective, committed, and coordinated efforts that would reflect positively on making the UN more effective and more responsive and inclusive for all. It will also reinforce its ability to address global emerging and complicated challenges. Madam President, GA Resolution 327/79/327 emphasized the important role of the GA, which is the most representative forum of the UN members. It also emphasized the principles of accountability, transparency, and multilateralism. The resolution also called for developing the working methods of the General Assembly and modernizing its tools to go along with current challenges and reinforce coordination between the main UN organs. In this context, my delegation welcomes the mentioning by the resolution of the need to reinforce gender representation in selecting the GA. The appointment of the Secretary-General is done by the GA upon the recommendation of the Security Council. Recent resolutions, including the current resolution, emphasize the need for more transparency and participation in this process. by allowing for all the member states to view the names of the candidates and to organize open debates between the candidates. These new practices, even if they do not change the legal framework provided for by the charter, reinforce the representation of the General Assembly and emphasizes its moral obligation to guarantee that the selection will be transparent and inclusive. Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reaffirms that the revitalization of the works of the GA is the first step towards a broader reform of the organization and contributes to reinforcing the principles of governance, transparency and accountability. It allows for an equal participation of all member states in discussing issues affecting peace, security, and development. Enabling the GA to discharge its full functions reinforces trust in the multilateral system. In this context, we emphasize the importance of complementarity between the roles of different UN organs and promoting coordination between the GA and the Security Council, which, in turn, is a main pillar to achieve coherence in UN decision-making. My country supports efforts aiming at promoting the principle of institutional complementarity and avoiding duplication to reinforce our shared vision and performance. We also consider that UN80 initiative is an important opportunity to unite our efforts and build an organization that is more coordinated and effective in facing global challenges. We also emphasize the need to move forward as member states and collectively with the adoption of measures within practical approaches to achieve our common goal as provided for by the Pact of the Future. It is important to reinforce the role of the General Assembly and to revitalize its works to make it more effective and responsive to global challenges in line with the UN Charter. We emphasize the central role of the General Assembly, which is the most representative organ of the United Nations and the main organ entrusted with policy making. In conclusion, we reaffirm that revitalizing the General Assembly is part and parcel of the ongoing efforts aiming at reinforcing the UN system as a whole to go along with the recent developments and to be more prepared to face the future. We look forward to pursuing our work and to supporting all efforts in this regard. and to preserve the momentum that was achieved and build on this momentum to achieve this important goal and make a greater progress and reach a wider consensus. Thank you, President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Saudi Arabia and now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Romania and former co-chair.

Madam President, Romania aligns with the statement delivered by the European Union, and I would like to add a few points. First of all, I'm very glad to witness one of the key deliverables of Resolution 79/3-7, which addresses the long overdue disparities in the translation among the six official languages of the UN on the use of gender-specific pronouns. Amending the rules of procedure to reflect female pronouns was long overdue, and I'm very glad that we can implement already from this 80th session this important decision by member states. Romania is proud to have contributed, together with South Africa, as co-chairs of the ad hoc working group on the revitalization of the General Assembly, to this important development, but also to a few other benchmarks contained in resolution 79/327. Just as we gather to debate on this item for the first time during the 80th session, we already see the preliminary results of the pledges we agreed upon in early September. Now in the peak of the committee season and All the main committees have already started and had their dedicated discussions on the working methods in accordance with operative paragraph 25 of this latest resolution. And you, Madam President, you have been a substantial part of the process, placing the implementation of the mandates on top of your agenda and also amplifying the efforts, amplifying this objective in your formal address at the start of each committee's work. I want to commend the efforts of the chairs and bureaus of the six committees, and we trust this exercise will foster more synergies and simplification in the way we operate, in sync with the broader UN80 reform objectives. I'm also aware that we need to inject more energy in the work of the committees to advance this important objective and to bring it to a meaningful outcome during the session. Madam President, my delegation is fully aligned with your vision of focusing on implementation of our commitments during this session. From working methods to the selection of a Secretary-General, the strength and impact of the mandates contained in 79/27 lay in creating the premises for their full and non-discretionary implementation. We are pleased to note the negotiations on the joint letter of the presidencies of the General Assembly and the Security Council are underway. We trust that both entities will make best use of the clearer and more structured steps for the Secretary-General selection process codified in OP 42, and we look forward to the formal kickstart of the process. Of course, the resolution states very clearly that the process should start in the last quarter of the year. I want to note that we are in the middle of this quarter and the process hasn't formally started, and I hope that we will see results soon on this part of the process as well. We are pleased to see member states are guided by the strong appeal to nominate women candidates as a first meaningful step for ensuring equality of chances in the lead up to the formal selection and appointment process for the next Secretary General. Madam President, the working group has been working for the past two sessions on refining the membership's approach to mandate delivery and mandate review. which is extremely timely in the context of the ongoing UN80 reform debates. We are pleased to see that several mitigation measures contained in Resolution 179327, particularly on the periodicity of resolutions and the overcrowding of the General Assembly agenda, represent a baseline for the ongoing discussions under UN80. We are encouraged by the several steps ahead we achieved through this resolution, and we hope the same constructive spirit and meaningful engagement among delegations will accompany the way forward in the UN80 reform process. On this particular note, it is worth recalling that we are not starting from scratch. The recently adopted resolution has established generally applicable criteria for resolutions adopted by this body, guided by the principle of the perennial nature of mandates of such resolutions until their operational scope has been fully implemented. and conveying a strong call to member states for reducing the number, length, and frequency based on an individual assessment against this criteria by each member state or group of member states applicable from the 81st session. Among the concrete decisions that we have undertaken in early September, I want to highlight that we have decided to limit to a maximum of three high-level meetings on the margins of the high-level week applicable from the 81st session. We also have a simplified mechanism that was mentioned by some colleagues, the one-gavel approach, not to repeat the procedure in adopting resolutions in the main committees, the plenary. But we also have a moratorium on international days and weeks and months during the 81st and 82nd session. And of course, you are all familiar with these decisions that we have undertaken, it's important to start implementing them in good faith. To conclude, Madam President, Romania will continue to be an active contributor to all efforts and in all fora aimed at successfully adapting this organization to meet the multifaceted challenges of today's multilateral architecture. And we remain committed to your efforts, Madam President, in ensuring that we Member States fulfill the commitments we have undertaken. Thank you very much.

I thank the distinguished representative of Romania. We have heard the last speaker in the debate on these items for this meeting. We shall hear the remaining speaker this afternoon at 3 p.m. in this hall. The meeting is until then adjourned.
